name: Italian Game
blurb: A classic answer to 1...e5 where White's bishop goes to c4 and aims at f7. This course plays the Giuoco Piano with c3 and d4, and the calm 4.d3 against the Two Knights Defense.

ideas.e4: Takes a central square and opens lines for the queen and the light-squared bishop.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3: Develops the knight and attacks the e5 pawn straight away, so Black has to spend a move defending it.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4: The bishop aims at f7, the square beside Black's king that only the king defends. Many attacks in this opening start there.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3: Prepares d4. With a pawn on c3, White can push d4 and keep a pawn in the centre after any exchanges.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4: Strikes in the centre and attacks both the e5 pawn and the bishop on c5.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd: Recaptures with the c-pawn, so White now has two pawns side by side on d4 and e4.
Blocks the check with the bishop and offers a trade. This is the calm choice; Nc3 instead leads to sharp gambit play.
Recaptures with the knight, which develops and protects the e4 pawn.
Gains space and chases the c6 knight away from the centre.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4: Against the quieter ...d6, the same plan: push d4 and claim the centre.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3: Against the Two Knights, White calmly protects e4 instead of starting tactics. The d3 pawn also opens a path for the c1 bishop.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 c3: Prepares d4 for later, a slow but healthy plan that keeps the centre under control.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Be7 O-O: Castles early. The centre is closed enough that getting the king safe comes first.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7 d4: Against the quiet Hungarian Defense, White uses the extra space at once and opens the centre.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxd4: Takes the knight that jumped forward. The trap behind ...Nd4 only works if White grabs e5 instead.
